mechaber/1:main: The laws of matzah mitzvah. And in it are 7 seifim: One should not knead matzah mitzvah nor bake it via an akum, nor via a cheresh, shoteh, or katan.
mechaber/2:main: The Rosh would exert himself regarding matzah mitzvah and stand over its production, urge those working and assist them in flattening them; and similarly it is fitting for every person to involve himself in the mitzvah personally.
mechaber/3:main: One who kneads after the time when chametz becomes forbidden should say at the time of kneading regarding all crumbs that fall at the time of kneading and flattening, and dough that clings to vessels: I annul them — so that when they are found, they will have been annulled before chametzing.
mechaber/4:main: One does not do sarikin that are painted, that is, to paint with a pate like an animal or a fowl, but everything that is done with a comb so that it does not swell, as well as what is between the matzahs, is permissible and it is good to hurry to do them, not to linger over them: he thought, and the matzats should be made thin and not thick like the rest of the bread, because there is no rush to miss the thin:
mechaber/5:main: One should not make on Pesach loaves a handbreadth thick.
mechaber/6:main: One should not be lenient regarding what the early authorities were strict about — not to make pandish or pladonish.
mechaber/7:main: One should not place whole eggs in matzah to bake together with them.
